Electrical and Computer Engineering
College of Engineering and Computer Science
Pursue a Career in R&D
Our PhD in Electrical, Electronics, and Computer Engineering at UM-Dearborn is a full-time, research-based degree designed to train students to conduct original, high quality translational research and develop innovative technologies in the fields of electrical, electronics, and computer engineering. We’ve designed the program primarily for students interested in research and development careers in industry or academia. It typically takes five years to complete.
To lessen financial concerns, all PhD students receive full funding in the form of appointments as a graduate student instructor, a research assistant, or both. The appointments provide a monthly stipend, health insurance, and a tuition waiver. Students are guaranteed full funding for up to five years provided they maintain good academic standing and adequate progress toward their degree.
Where a PhD in Electrical, Electronics, and Computer Engineering Will Take You
Numerous studies and survey data predict continued growth in engineering-related fields in the years to come. The PhD degree gives you the technical skills and professional development needed to excel in various career paths–whether that means diving into high-tech start-ups, leading projects in established engineering companies, or even pushing the boundaries of technology while pursuing an academic career.

Electrical and Electronics Engineers
Overall employment of electrical and electronics engineers is projected to grow 8 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.
About 16,300 openings for electrical and electronics engineers are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.
